summary: The Android manifest reveals multiple exported components (activities, service, receiver, and content provider) lacking protection, with debug mode enabled and backup allowed, exposing the app to an expanded attack surface that includes data leaks, unintended inter‑app communication, and privilege misuse.
attack_surface: Exported content provider ContentProviderActivity with public authority
top_risks: Unprotected exported components may be triggered by malicious apps
Accessible backup/restore may lead to data leakage
Unrestricted external storage access allows data exfiltration
Public content provider exposes internal data
abuse_hypotheses: External app starts SplashActivity to invoke internal logic
Malicious app reads/writes to external storage to defect data
Unprotected service receives malicious intents to trigger downloads
Receiver hijacking to send arbitrary intents
Content provider queried to export sensitive application data
recommended_next_steps: Mark exported components as non‑exported or protect them with <uses-permission> or <exported> with required permission
Disable android:debuggable and remove allowBackup=true in release builds
Restrict WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with requestLegacyExternalStorage or scoped storage
Implement permission checks within exported service and receiver
Add authentication and authority restrictions to content provider
